tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: In the matter of Popular Mega Motors (India) Private Limited (PMMIL) (Wholly Owned Subsidiary): Assessment order was issued by the Department for the Financial Year 2008-09. PMMIL filed a writ petition before the Hon'ble High Court challenging the said order. The appeal grounds are: (a) Assessment was done after the expiry of the period as prescribed under the KVAT Act (time-barred by limitation), and (b) Merit of the case. The Court favourably decided similar cases in favour of the assessees, and the Department filed appeals before the Division Bench against the said judgments. In our case, the appeal filed by the Department was under consideration before the Hon'ble Court. The Court granted a stay in the subject matter, and the same has been pending for disposal for over a period of 3 years.

tax_litigation.status: The Hon'ble High Court granted stay on the order and the same is pending for disposal. There is no change from the previous disclosure.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: In the matter of Prabal Motors Private Limited (PMPL) (Subsidiary): PMPL received a Show Cause Notice from Additional Commissioner, Central Goods and Services Tax, Coimbatore dated 28/12/2023 alleging a difference of Rs.13.58 Crores between GSTR-2A and GSTR-3B for the financial year 2018-19. The difference was caused by an error made by Daimler India Commercial Vehicles Pvt. Ltd. Wherein the OEM incorrectly reported invoices for February and March 2019 under the taxpayer's old GSTIN and later corrected the mistake in May 2019 by amending the GSTR-1 returns. As a result, a mismatch arose between GSTR-2A and GSTR-3B. Drop Order Received on 28/03/2024. Form GST APL-03 Received on 27/09/2024. Order received on 11/06/2025. Review is allowed. The adjudicating authority is directed to comply with the direction of the CBIC Circular No.183115/2022-GST dated 27.12.2022 and pass a fresh order as per law.

timeline.summary: CRISIL Ratings reaffirmed subsidiary Popular Mega Motors' bank loan facilities of ₹235.55 Cr at CRISIL A/Stable / A1.
On 22 May 2026, Popular Vehicles and Services announced the resignation of CEO Raj Narayan, effective 21 August 2026.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹1,754.45 Cr, net loss ₹4.96 Cr (against a loss of ₹13.72 Cr a year earlier).
Popular Vehicles reported Q4FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹1,758.8 Cr, up 27.8% YoY, with EBITDA rising 93.5% to ₹57.5 Cr.
Popular Vehicles and Services Ltd made the audio recording of its Q4 FY2026 Investor & Analyst Conference Call available on its website on 2026-05-27.
On 27 May 2026 Popular Vehicles' Q4/FY26 call guided FY27 to high double-digit revenue growth, a 4.8-5% EBITDA margin and PAT near FY24 levels, with sustainable profitability from Q2FY27.
